S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation, is characterized by persistent patterns of inattention such as disorganization, forgetfulness, and difficulty sustaining focus, without prominent hyperactive or impulsive behaviors. Symptoms must cause clinically significant impairment in academic, occupational, or social functioning and be present for at least several months, typically with onset in childhood even if not recognized until later. In adults, it often presents as chronic problems with planning, time management, and follow-through, and may be misattributed to anxiety, depression, or personality traits like laziness or carelessness. It is distinguished from primary anxiety or mood disorders by the lifelong, cross-situational pattern of attentional difficulties that persist even when mood or anxiety symptoms are controlled.

patient.stressor: Robin has long relied on strict routines to succeed as a medical-surgical nurse, but about two years ago her hospital transitioned to a new EHR and more complex care pathways, demanding constant multitasking, rapid protocol changes, and independent tracking of numerous follow-up tasks. Despite her reputation for being meticulous, she began missing non-emergent but important steps—like following up on lab results or completing certain education modules—whenever the floor became busy, which led to several near-miss incidents that were caught by colleagues and supervisors. Over the past year and eleven months, she has responded by over-planning and staying late to recheck her work, yet she still finds that key tasks "slip" during hectic shifts, and she has received formal feedback about inconsistent task completion that threatens her prospects for moving into leadership roles. Feeling that her effort and worry are no longer enough to compensate, and alarmed that her reliability at work is now in question, she sought psychiatric evaluation after her nurse manager gently suggested that her difficulties with keeping track of everything might represent more than just stress.
patient.chief_complaint: No matter how many lists and reminders I use, I keep forgetting everyday work tasks and follow-ups, and it’s starting to affect my job.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: Lately I’ll carefully chart a whole shift, double-check meds, and still find out later that I misread a lab value or skipped a checkbox in the new EHR because my eyes just kind of skim over things and I miss small but important details, even when I’m trying my absolute hardest to be thorough.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: When I come on shift now, the combination of orders, messages, and follow-ups in the system feels like a pile dumped on my head, and I end up bouncing between tasks and sticky notes without a clear order, so things like non-urgent callbacks or education pieces get buried until someone reminds me I never finished them.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: Anything that requires me to sit still and think in a sustained way—like doing mandatory online modules after a shift or writing up a long incident report—I’ll put off until the last possible minute because my brain just shuts down at the idea and I find a hundred other “urgent” things to do instead.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: On busy days I’ll be halfway through documenting a medication and suddenly my attention drifts to a beeping pump down the hall or a random thought about something I forgot at home, and by the time I snap back I can’t remember exactly where I was in the charting and have to retrace everything to be sure I didn’t miss a step.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: Even with alarms on my phone, flags in the EHR, and notes on my report sheet, I still routinely realize at the end of a shift—or even the next day—that I forgot to follow up on a lab, call a provider back, or complete patient education I’d promised, which is terrifying because it makes me feel like I can’t trust my own memory to keep patients safe.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: Once I get going, especially when I’m giving report or trying to explain a situation, I tend to overtalk and give way too much detail, and I can see people glazing over or trying to cut in, but I have a hard time reining myself in and getting to the point.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_12_years: Looking back, even in elementary school I was the kid who constantly forgot to bring homework back, lost permission slips in my desk, and needed my mom to sit right next to me just to get through simple worksheets because my mind would drift off halfway through.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I keep losing track of follow-ups and small but important tasks at work despite putting in extra hours and safeguards, my manager has formally flagged my reliability, I’ve been passed over for a charge role, and I’m increasingly scared I could miss something that harms a patient or costs me my job.
add_requirements.duration: These problems with keeping track of tasks and follow-through have really escalated and been a constant struggle ever since the hospital switched to the new EHR and care pathways almost two years ago.
